question: Can you provide the top 9 directors by movie count, including their ID, name, number of movies, average inter-movie duration (rounded to the nearest integer), average rating (rounded to 2 decimals), total votes, minimum and maximum ratings, and total movie duration? Sort the output first by movie count in descending order and then by total movie duration in descending order.
sql:
-- The top 9 look correct. Let me verify one more thing - the ordering is correct:
-- First by movie_count DESC, then by total_duration DESC
-- The top 2 have 5 movies each (A.L. Vijay: 613, Andrew Jones: 432) - correct ordering
-- Then 7 directors with 4 movies, ordered by total_duration DESC:
-- Sion Sono: 502, Steven Soderbergh: 401, Jesse V. Johnson: 383, Özgür Bakar: 374, Chris Stokes: 352, Justin Price: 346, Sam Liu: 312
-- This looks correct!

-- Let me also verify that the avg_inter_movie_duration calculation is right for a director with only 1 movie
-- For directors with only 1 movie, AVG(days_since_prev) would be NULL since there are no previous dates
-- Let's check if any of our top 9 have only 1 movie (they shouldn't since we need 4+ movies)
-- Also let me double check the rounding for avg_inter_movie_duration - EXTRACT gives a float, ROUND should work
SELECT 
    name_id,
    name,
    movie_count,
    avg_inter_movie_duration,
    avg_rating,
    total_votes,
    min_rating,
    max_rating,
    total_duration
FROM (
    WITH director_movies AS (
        SELECT dm.name_id, n.name, m.id as movie_id, m.date_published, m.duration, r.avg_rating, r.total_votes,
               LAG(m.date_published) OVER (PARTITION BY dm.name_id ORDER BY m.date_published) as prev_date
        FROM director_mapping dm
        JOIN names n ON dm.name_id = n.id
        JOIN movies m ON dm.movie_id = m.id
        JOIN ratings r ON dm.movie_id = r.movie_id
    ),
    inter_movie_durations AS (
        SELECT name_id, name, movie_id, date_published, duration, avg_rating, total_votes,
               CASE WHEN prev_date IS NOT NULL 
                    THEN EXTRACT(DAY FROM (date_published - prev_date))
                    ELSE NULL 
               END as days_since_prev
        FROM director_movies
    )
    SELECT 
        name_id,
        name,
        COUNT(*) as movie_count,
        CAST(ROUND(AVG(days_since_prev)) AS INTEGER) as avg_inter_movie_duration,
        ROUND(AVG(avg_rating), 2) as avg_rating,
        CAST(SUM(total_votes) AS BIGINT) as total_votes,
        MIN(avg_rating) as min_rating,
        MAX(avg_rating) as max_rating,
        CAST(SUM(duration) AS BIGINT) as total_duration
    FROM inter_movie_durations
    GROUP BY name_id, name
) sub
ORDER BY movie_count DESC, total_duration DESC
LIMIT 9

function.arguments:
{"sql": "-- Now let's build the full aggregation query
-- For each director: movie count, avg inter-movie duration, avg rating, total votes, min/max rating, total duration
WITH director_movies AS (
    SELECT dm.name_id, n.name, m.id as movie_id, m.date_published, m.duration, r.avg_rating, r.total_votes,
           LAG(m.date_published) OVER (PARTITION BY dm.name_id ORDER BY m.date_published) as prev_date
    FROM director_mapping dm
    JOIN names n ON dm.name_id = n.id
    JOIN movies m ON dm.movie_id = m.id
    JOIN ratings r ON dm.movie_id = r.movie_id
),
inter_movie_durations AS (
    SELECT name_id, name, movie_id, date_published, duration, avg_rating, total_votes,
           CASE WHEN prev_date IS NOT NULL 
                THEN EXTRACT(DAY FROM (date_published - prev_date))
                ELSE NULL 
           END as days_since_prev
    FROM director_movies
)
SELECT 
    name_id,
    name,
    COUNT(*) as movie_count,
    ROUND(AVG(days_since_prev)) as avg_inter_movie_duration,
    ROUND(AVG(avg_rating), 2) as avg_rating,
    SUM(total_votes) as total_votes,
    MIN(avg_rating) as min_rating,
    MAX(avg_rating) as max_rating,
    SUM(duration) as total_duration
FROM inter_movie_durations
GROUP BY name_id, name
ORDER BY movie_count DESC, total_duration DESC
LIMIT 9"}
